title: Following Algorithms and Building Trace Tables
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: What drives decisions in spiral development?
questions.answer: Identification, assessment and mitigation of risk.
options: Identification, assessment and mitigation of risk.
Identification, assessment OR mitigation of risk.
There is not enough information to determine the result.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Identification, assessment and mitigation of risk.

questions.prompt: Why can an array provide direct indexed access?
questions.answer: Its element locations can be calculated from base address and index.
options: Its element locations can be calculated from base address OR index.
Its element locations cannot be calculated from base address and index.
Its element locations can be calculated from base address and index.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Its element locations can be calculated from base address and index.

questions.prompt: A full adder receives A=1, B=1 and carry-in=0. What are sum and carry-out?
For the binary value 1010, what is its decimal value?

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: trace table — Record of algorithm state as steps execute.
dry run — Manual simulation of algorithm.
boundary test — Test at edge of valid input domain.

blocks.title: Identify state
blocks.text: Find variables, data structures, conditions and inputs.

blocks.title: Trace each step
blocks.text: Update a table when an assignment or state change occurs. For a recursive function, record each call, its argument and its eventual return value; unlike a loop, calls wait on the call stack.

blocks.title: Check outcome
blocks.text: Compare output against constraints and edge cases. Recursion must reach a base case that returns without another recursive call, or it cannot terminate safely.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model answer
blocks.text: At n=1 total 0; n=2 total 2; n=3 total 2; n=4 total 6; output 6. Record n and total at each loop step. Check: link each claim to the scenario and use precise OCR terminology.

blocks.title: Worked example · Spot the stopping condition
blocks.text: n == 0 is the base case: return 0 immediately. Otherwise SumTo(n - 1) invokes the same method with a smaller argument. Assume n is non-negative.

blocks.text: Progress: initial 0; after 3 → 3; after 8 → 8; after 5 stays 8; final output 8. The initial zero fails if all values are negative; use first element instead.
